findings.note: Unchecked type assertion in finish(): env["untrusted"].([]string) at envelope.go:192 panics if any caller ever stores untrusted as a different slice type (e.g. []any). Every current caller in run.go uses []string, and the sibling read at envelope.go:220 correctly uses the comma-ok form, so this is latent inconsistency rather than a live bug, but a panic here escapes as an unstructured crash on the stdout-JSON contract.

evidence.note: env["untrusted"] = appendSorted(env["untrusted"].([]string), "warnings[].detail") — no comma-ok, unlike line 220.

findings.note: tests/coverage.sh:46 rebuilds bin/metareview in the EXIT trap to undo the -cover instrumentation, but a failure of that rebuild is invisible: bash keeps the pre-trap exit status, so the gate can print 'coverage gate passed' and exit 0 while leaving an instrumented bin/metareview (the npm-packaged entry point) in the tree. A `|| echo ... >&2` or an explicit exit in cleanup would make the state visible.

evidence.note: cleanup() { rm -rf "$COVDIR"; go build -o bin/metareview ./cmd/metareview; } — trap cleanup EXIT; failure is swallowed.

findings.note: The 100%-coverage case pattern at tests/coverage.sh:85 is `internal/fsm/*|workflows`, which does not match a top-level `internal/fsm` package. Such a package would be required to be present in the profile (line 39 check) but would fall through to the floor branch and report 'no floor' — unenforced — contradicting the header comment that every package in `go list ./internal/fsm/...` must report 100.0%. No such package exists today (go list returns 13 subpackages plus workflows), so this is latent; `internal/fsm|internal/fsm/*|workflows` closes it.
